For example, suppose a loan is characterized by its interest rate rl, the loan amount L, and the collateral the lender requires C. An increase in the loan rate rl increases x’, and this implies that some borrowers with less risky projects will find it unprofitable to borrow if the loan rate rises, while borrowers with riskier projects will still find it worthwhile to borrow. Because the borrower can lose no more than his collateral in the bad state, expected profits are a convex function of the project’s return and therefore increase with an increase in risk (for a constant mean return).
